Candy Apples

Served at: All Hallows' Eve (Halloween)

Serves 8Prep 15 minCook 10 min

Candy apples are a classic Halloween treat, symbolizing the festive spirit of All Hallows' Eve. These glossy, sweet-coated apples are enjoyed by children and adults alike, often found at Halloween parties and fall fairs.

Ingredients

  • 8 medium apples (Granny Smith or Fuji)
  • 8 wooden sticks
  • 2 cups granulated sugar (400 g)
  • 1/2 cup light corn syrup (120 ml)
  • 3/4 cup water (180 ml)
  • 1/2 teaspoon red food coloring
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract (optional)

Method

  1. Wash and thoroughly dry the apples; remove stems and insert wooden sticks into the top of each apple.
  2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat and set aside.
  3. In a medium saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, and water over medium heat; stir until sugar dissolves.
  4. Attach a candy thermometer to the pan and bring the mixture to a boil without stirring until it reaches 300°F (149°C), the hard crack stage.
  5. Remove the pan from heat and quickly stir in the red food coloring and vanilla extract if using.
  6. Working quickly, dip each apple into the hot candy mixture, turning to coat evenly; allow excess to drip off.
  7. Place the coated apples on the prepared baking sheet to cool and harden completely, about 30 minutes.
  8. Once set, serve immediately or store in a cool, dry place.

Tips

  • Use fresh, firm apples for the best texture and flavor.
  • If the candy mixture hardens before you finish dipping, gently reheat it to maintain the right consistency.
  • For extra flair, roll the coated apples in chopped nuts, sprinkles, or crushed candy before the coating sets.
